questions.stem: In a survey of 90 students, 30 chose football. What angle should the football sector be on a pie chart?
questions.explanation: Angle = (frequency / total) x 360 = (30/90) x 360 = 120°. Option (a) uses the frequency as the angle. Always multiply the fraction by 360°.

questions.stem: A pie chart has a sector of 45° for 'Bus'. If the chart represents 160 students, how many travel by bus?
questions.explanation: Frequency = (angle / 360) x total = (45/360) x 160 = 1/8 x 160 = 20. Option (a) uses the angle as the frequency.

questions.stem: A pie chart showing favourite fruits has: Apples 100°, Bananas 80°, Oranges 60°, Grapes ?°. What is the angle for Grapes?
questions.explanation: All angles must sum to 360°. Grapes = 360 - 100 - 80 - 60 = 120°.

questions.stem: Two pie charts compare favourite sports. Chart A (200 students) has football at 90°. Chart B (300 students) has football at 72°. Which group has more football fans?
questions.explanation: Group A: (90/360) x 200 = 50. Group B: (72/360) x 300 = 60. Although Group A has a larger angle, Group B has more football fans because the total is larger. You cannot compare angles directly when totals differ.

questions.stem: A pie chart represents 180 people. The sector for 'Car' is 80°. How many more people would need to choose 'Car' for its sector to become 120°, if the total stays 180?
questions.explanation: Current 'Car' = (80/360) x 180 = 40 people. Needed for 120° = (120/360) x 180 = 60 people. Additional = 60 - 40 = 20 people. Note: the total stays at 180, so these extra people must switch from other categories.
